analysis_kind: exploratory continuation; same simulator cases previously inspected
question: Does resuming the 500-update LoRA checkpoint to 2000 cumulative updates improve paired LIBERO Object success?
hypothesis: More optimizer updates may reduce imitation error and improve task completion; proxy loss may improve without success.
primary_metric: LIBERO completed-task count out of 10; one same initial-state per task
restore: Full params and AdamW optimizer state via official checkpoint restore; replay and verify first 500 frame sampler draws; official flow RNG folded by restored global step.
learning_rate: Preserve original warmup-cosine schedule including decay_steps=500; clamped floor 1e-5 for updates 501-2000; no restart/warmup.
fixed: Original data split (40 train/10 val trajectories), training-only normalization, model/config, batch=1, seed=42, all original weights frozen, evaluator/controller/initial states.
diagnostic: Same 10 midpoint frames per split; fixed noise; not full validation loss.
stop: Stop at global update 2000 and one valid 10-task evaluation. Abort nonfinite numerics/infrastructure failures; retain evidence. No automatic extension.
selection: Evaluate predeclared final checkpoint; no checkpoint selection by success.
uncertainty: Single training seed and one episode per task; descriptive paired case counts only, no generalization inference.
limitations: No audited disjointness between simulator initial states and expert collection states.
Repeated use of the same 10 cases makes this exploratory.
A continuation at the original low learning-rate floor is not equivalent to a fresh 2000-step cosine schedule.
